articles.body: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=v1zMt0-aJKw Google’s Pixel Tag is finally going on sale, three months after it debuted alongside the Pixel 11 series. It’s the company’s own answer to Apple’s AirTag, and like the AirTag, it leans on a huge crowdsourced network to help you find whatever you attach it to. In this case, that’s Google’s Find Hub network , which the company says spans over a billion Android devices. I’ve been testing the Pixel Tag with my Pixel 11 Pro , and rather than just pinging it around the house, I deliberately lost my keys twice: once on a busy downtown street and once at a quiet, wooded trailhead. Here’s how it held up, and what you should know before you buy one.

articles.title: Were there 'lost cosmonauts' in the early Soviet space program?
articles.excerpt: At the height of the Cold War, two amateur radio operators alleged they intercepted signals from Soviet cosmonauts who perished during missions that remained secret.
articles.body: In the final weeks of 1960, two young radio enthusiasts were monitoring transmissions from a home-built listening station on a rooftop in Turin, Italy, when the brothers detected something extraordinary: a faint signal that bore the hallmarks of one originating from space. That wasn't the only surprising thing about the alleged signal:, the transmission carried a very familiar message: it was Morse code for the international distress signal SOS. As the youths listened, the signal seemed to grow weaker. This raised a troubling possibility: could it be that the signal's source was moving farther away from Earth ?

articles.title: Store Timestamps in UTC, Display Them Locally
articles.excerpt: A CRM stores '10:30' beside a follow-up task. One representative reads it in Jaipur and another in London. Neither knows which timezone the value represents. Time data needs to describe either an inst…
articles.body: A CRM stores '10:30' beside a follow-up task. One representative reads it in Jaipur and another in London. Neither knows which timezone the value represents. Time data needs to describe either an instant or a local scheduling intention. Those are different requirements. Store instants unambiguously An enquiry acceptance time is an instant. Store it using a timezone-aware database type or an explicit UTC representation supported by your system. JavaScript can serialize a valid Date as a UTC ISO string: const acceptedAt = new Date (); const timestamp = acceptedAt . toISOString (); This records the browser or server clock's value. For authoritative acceptance time, prefer the backend's timestamp and maintain its clock synchronization.

articles.body: You start an agent on the computer at home and leave. An hour later your phone shows that it stopped to ask for permission to run a command. They just don't work the same way: Claude Code: run /remote-control in the session, then open it in the Claude app or at claude.ai/code. It needs a Pro, Max, Ultra, Team, or Enterprise plan. Codex: set up Control this Mac or PC in the ChatGPT desktop app, pair your phone with the QR code, and answer from the ChatGPT mobile app. Any agent: turn on SSH on the computer, reach it from outside your network, and keep the agent in tmux . articles.title: UUIDv4 Is Not Free: Why Random Primary Keys Are Silently Crushing Your Write Performance
articles.excerpt: When my database write latency spiked by 340% after crossing 50 million rows, my CPU wasn't maxed out. My queries weren't missing indexes. Instead, my storage IOPS was completely saturated by a single…
articles.body: When my database write latency spiked by 340% after crossing 50 million rows, my CPU wasn't maxed out. My queries weren't missing indexes. Instead, my storage IOPS was completely saturated by a single architectural default I set up on day one: using UUIDv4 as my primary key. Most backend engineers avoid auto-incrementing integers ( BIGINT / SERIAL ) in public-facing systems for good reasons. Sequential IDs leak business metrics, enable enumeration attacks ( /api/orders/1042 , /api/orders/1043 ), and make distributed ID generation across microservices painful. So I reached for the industry standard: UUIDv4 . It is 128 bits of randomness, requires zero coordination between nodes, and guarantees global uniqueness.

articles.title: NASA Scientists Show How Gravitational Waves Can Reveal New Worlds
articles.excerpt: The LISA (Laser Interferometer Space Antenna) observatory, now in development, will detect gravitational waves, the tiny ripples in space-time caused by orbiting masses. Now two studies led by NASA as…
articles.body: 5 min read NASA Scientists Show How Gravitational Waves Can Reveal New Worlds The LISA (Laser Interferometer Space Antenna) observatory, now in development, will detect gravitational waves, the tiny ripples in space-time caused by orbiting masses. Now two studies led by NASA astrophysicists show in new detail how LISA could reveal a new and unique population of exoplanets — worlds beyond our solar system — throughout our galaxy. Watch to learn how the presence of a planet modifies the gravitational wave signal from tightly orbiting white dwarfs. The LISA (Laser Interferometer Space Antenna) observatory could detect a Jupiter-mass planet in such systems up to thousands of light-years away.

articles.body: A robot just played Tinkertoys in space, assembling the first satellite structure ever made without a human touching the controls. The DARPA-funded project saw a robotic "truss builder" create a reflective antenna using Kapton film, composite fiber tubes and aluminum joints. The implications are huge for future missions, potentially opening up new possibilities to build — or fix — satellites in the final frontier. "This is the first time that a structure has been autonomously constructed in space ," Sergio Pellegrino, an aerospace and civil engineering professor at the California Institute of Technology (Caltech), said in a statement on Nov. 5 .

articles.excerpt: The Crew Health and Performance Exploration Analog (CHAPEA) Mission 2 crew arranged photos around a boot print in the simulated Martian sand outside their habitat on Aug. 31, 2026. The crew recently e…
articles.body: NASA The Crew Health and Performance Exploration Analog (CHAPEA) Mission 2 crew arranged photos around a boot print in the simulated Martian sand outside their habitat on Aug. 31, 2026. The crew recently exited their habitat on Saturday, Oct. 31, after 378 days of isolation in a facility at the agency’s Johnson Space Center in Houston. Health and performance data collected from the simulation can help NASA develop methods to counter human spaceflight risks for future Artemis and Moon Base missions. Image credit: NASA

articles.title: Anthropic targets $1.4 trillion IPO
articles.excerpt: Anthropic confirmed on Tuesday that its IPO could be one of the biggest ever, even while falling short of previous expectations. Its IPO price is expected to be between $70.00 and $78.00 per share, wh…
articles.body: Anthropic confirmed on Tuesday that its IPO could be one of the biggest ever, even while falling short of previous expectations. Its IPO price is expected to be between $70.00 and $78.00 per share, which would put its valuation as high as $1.4 trillion, according to the The New York Times . The Wall Street Journal reports that according to its sources, Anthropic is "aiming for its shares to start trading Thursday or Friday next week." As Reuters notes, the Anthropic IPO was previously expected to be valued at as much as $2 trillion. As of last week, Anthropic's rival OpenAI was valued at $1.25 trillion . articles.title: See the first images from the new ZWO Seestar S30 Plus — a smart telescope aimed at beginners
articles.excerpt: While rivals announce increasingly expensive smart telescopes, ZWO’s new Seestar S30 Plus makes galaxy and nebula photography surprisingly affordable.
articles.body: As rival makers announce increasingly ambitious smart telescopes , ZWO has taken a different approach. Its new Seestar S30 Plus launched today and is available for $474 from Seestar’s website and Amazon , just in time for Christmas. Better still, we’ve been using it for a month and can bring you a first look. Announced a few months after the flagship Seestar S50 Pro and replacing the now-discontinued Seestar S30 , the new Seestar S30 Plus retains its 30mm aperture and compact chassis, but upgrades to four-element apochromatic optics with extra-low dispersion (ED) glass and two 3.7-megapixel cameras. The ZWO Seestar S30 Plus is a new sub-$500 smart telescope with upgraded optics and dual 3.7MP cameras.
